metadata.description: A bounded theoretical and methods preprint analyzing uneven recognition and access during AI transitions. Distinguishes actual opportunity to shape decisions from eventual awareness, AI use, and intellectual production. It derives finite matching-based identification bounds and their inverse, the minimum materially effective choice-window extension guaranteeing a target count under unknown pairings; includes recovery/irreversibility counterexamples, scoped exact tests, and a prospective empirical design. The mathematics explicitly inherits classical fixed-marginal matching, anticipatory governance and option-preservation work. Not a survey of actual populations, an AI timeline forecast, a real governance experiment, or independent validation of civilizational discontinuity. ChatGPT substantially assisted under human direction; not peer reviewed.
metadata.notes: First public version of the CD-v1.0.0/CD-v1.1.0 manuscript family, not an update of the distinct published CIPSA or Guardians research. Claims and external precedent limited as detailed in supplementary source review. Human author of record Hongju Liu; substantial AI assistance and lack of independent peer review disclosed.
metadata.title: Awareness Can Catch Up After Choice Has Closed: Uneven Readiness, Effective Reconsideration, and Civilizational Desynchronization in AI Transitions

scientific_status: Conditional theory; not peer reviewed or real world observational data
